title: Type conversion and why Go never converts on your behalf

videos.script: Lesson 9 finished the basic types. This lesson is about what happens when two of them meet. {{mismatch}} Add an int to an int64 and Go refuses to build. Multiply a price by a count and it refuses again. Other languages would widen one side and carry on. Go makes you write the conversion yourself. {{conversions}} So the next thing is what a conversion does. Some are harmless. Some cut a float down to its whole part. Some keep the low bits of an integer and throw the rest away, without a word. And one, from an int to a string, does something almost nobody expects. {{strconv}} Turning text into a number is not a conversion at all. It is a function that can fail, and it tells you when it does. {{named}} Last, your own types. A Celsius and a Fahrenheit can both be float64 underneath and still refuse to add. That refusal is the point. By the end you will know why every conversion in a Go program is written down where you can see it.
